ai.description: *Cnemaspis andersonii* reaches a snout-vent length of 45 mm. It is brown with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and possesses keeled ventral scales. The species lacks a precloacal pore.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis andersonii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, keeled tubercles on the flanks, which are absent in most similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis andersonii* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Eastern Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces and tree trunks at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis andersonii* is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks during the brightest hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis andersonii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis andersonii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
